summary.oneLiner: Among India's leading agrochemical companies, delivering technology-driven crop protection solutions (insecticides, fungicides, herbicides and biostimulants) to farmers pan-India through a deep distribution network and MNC technology partnerships.
summary.business: Dhanuka Agritech Limited is one of India's leading agrochemical companies, developing, manufacturing and marketing crop protection products (insecticides, fungicides, herbicides) and allied agri-inputs such as biofertilizers/biostimulants for Indian farmers. It operates four manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses, reaching over 10 million farmers through around 6,500 distributors and more than 80,000 retailers, and partners with ten multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the United States to bring differentiated chemistries to the Indian market.

risks.note: Near-term demand visibility remains contingent on monsoon progression and reservoir levels; localized weather disruptions and climatic anomalies (including El Niño-related impacts) could influence agricultural activity, crop health and pesticide consumption patterns across regions.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption to energy/trade and input supply chains
risks.note: Geopolitical tensions in key regions, including the Middle East (Iran-Israel conflict, potential disruption around the Strait of Hormuz) and the Gulf region, pose risks to global energy and trade markets; escalation may raise crude oil, freight, fertiliser and raw material prices and increase input costs.

risks.risk: Input cost and commodity price volatility
risks.note: Volatility in global fertiliser, energy and commodity prices remains a key monitorable that can pressure input costs and margins.
Global agrochemical markets are only gradually stabilizing after an extended inventory correction cycle, indicating continued channel/demand volatility risk.

risks.risk: Macro, currency, competitive and regulatory risk
risks.note: Cautionary statement flags general market and macro-economic trends, movements in currency exchange and interest rates, competitive pressures, technological developments, changes in financial condition of counterparties, and legislative/regulatory developments as factors that could cause results to differ from expectations.
The Risk Management Committee explicitly monitors informational and cybersecurity risks alongside financial, operational and sectoral risks as part of its risk management policy.

risks.risk: Channel liquidity and uneven crop economics
risks.note: The broader agrochemical operating environment faced pressure from erratic weather patterns, uneven crop economics and weak channel liquidity in certain regions during the year, with the Rabi season additionally affected by unfavourable climatic conditions in certain key regions.

one-line thesis: Dhanuka reported resilient Q4FY26 growth (9% revenue, 33% PAT) driven by product mix and a significant Rs 14.5cr GST refund one-off, masking underlying margin pressures from rising input costs. Guidance for FY27 remains constructive (low double-digit growth) despite a projected 100bps margin contraction due to the absence of the GST benefit and higher raw material costs, with growth optionality tied to Bayer product integration and herbicide demand from labor shortages.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs 483.34cr (+9% YoY); EBITDA: Rs 124.89cr (+14% YoY), Margin ~25.8% (inflated by one-off); PAT: Rs 97.77cr (+29.5% YoY); Order Book: N/A (FMCG-style agri sales); Net Debt: Strong cash position, Rs 70cr buyback approved. One-offs: Rs 14.5cr GST refund in Q4 (Rs 29cr full year) artificially boosted margins; Other expenses down 49% YoY in Q4 due to cost control and increased principal support.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: Low double digits; Margin: Expected decline of ~100bps (ex-one-off); Order Inflow: Positive Kharif outlook driven by oilseed/pulse acreage; Capex: Focus on backward integration for Bayer molecules at Dahej.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for formulation business; Channel inventory reported as healthy with no significant carryover from Rabi.
segment / subsidiary detail: Insecticides (41%), Herbicides (31%), Fungicides (14%), Others (14%). Zone mix: North (32%), South (33%), West (23%), East (12%). Dahej unit revenue Rs 50cr (vs guided Rs 65cr), EBITDA loss Rs 13cr.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Full integration of Bayer molecules (Triadimenol, Iprovalicarb) with formulation shifting to India; 2) Herbicide volume growth driven by structural labor shortages forcing mechanization/weedicide use; 3) Biostimulant recovery to >Rs 130cr after regulatory ban impact.
margins & cost dynamics: Input costs up 3-5% basket-wide (imported tech +5-6%, domestic generic +15-30%). Company plans to pass on 2% in Q1 and 3-4% in Q2. Gross margins expected to normalize ex-GST refund; carryover inventory provides temporary cushion.
capex / expansion: Backward integration for Bayer products at Dahej facility; Triadimenol formulation shifting to India in FY27, Iprovalicarb technical production starting end of FY27.
capital allocation: Dividend: 100% (Rs 2/share); Buyback: Up to Rs 70cr at Rs 1,400/share (~25% premium); ESOP scheme approved for employee alignment.
risks & watch-items: 1) Monsoon volatility impacting sowing; 2) Persistent input cost inflation unable to be passed through; 3) Delays in international registrations for Bayer products; 4) Regulatory changes in biostimulants.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and cash flows; Pragmatic on near-term margin headwinds and Dahej underperformance; Transparent on one-off benefits.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly cited 'labor shortage' as a perpetual structural driver for herbicide demand, expanding into traditional labor-surplus states (Bihar, UP). The Dahej unit revenue guidance was downgraded to Rs 75cr for FY27 (from earlier Rs 100cr expectations) due to slow international registration despite domestic robustness.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs and margin compression ex-one-off | Generic Agrochemical Formulators | loser | Med | Smaller players without hedging or pricing power will struggle to pass on 3-5% cost inflation compared to Dhanuka's branded portfolio. |
| Labor shortage driving herbicide adoption | Herbicide Specialists | beneficiary | High | Structural shift from manual weeding to chemical solutions benefits companies with strong weedicides portfolio like Dhanuka. |
| Regulatory clarity post-ban | Organized Biostimulant Players | beneficiary | Med | Market recovering from regulatory ban; organized players with registered products (like Dhanuka's new launches) gain share from unorganized exit. |

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dhanuka Agritech Limited is one of India's leading agrochemical companies, developing, manufacturing and marketing crop protection products (insecticides, fungicides, herbicides) and allied agri-inputs such as biofertilizers/biostimulants for Indian farmers. It operates four manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses, reaching over 10 million farmers through around 6,500 distributors and more than 80,000 retailers, and partners with ten multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the United States to bring differentiated chemistries to the Indian market.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Near-term demand visibility remains contingent on monsoon progression and reservoir levels; the Company remains constructive on the medium-to-long-term structural growth prospects of Indian agriculture and crop production
- The Rabi season in FY26 was additionally affected by unfavourable climatic conditions in certain key regions; climate variability (unseasonal rainfall, temperature fluctuations, shifting monsoon patterns) continues to influence sowing behaviour, crop productivity, input demand and farmer sentiment
- Broader agrochemical industry operating environment remained challenging during the year — pressure from erratic weather patterns, uneven crop economics and weak channel liquidity in certain regions, with global commodity/supply-chain volatility further accentuated in March 2026 by geopolitical developments in the Gulf region
- Rising Minimum Support Prices (MSP) across key crops (paddy, maize, tur, moong, urad, groundnut, soybean, cotton) during FY23-FY25 are expected to encourage acreage expansion and input intensity, supporting agrochemical demand over the medium term
- Global pesticides market grew from ~USD 51.5bn (CY20) to ~USD 72.3bn (CY25), a ~7% CAGR, and is projected to reach ~USD 103.9bn by CY30 (~8% CAGR CY25-CY30), driven by adoption of advanced crop-protection chemicals, expansion of commercial farming and rising penetration of biological/sustainable pesticide solutions
- India's pesticide exports remained significantly higher than imports during FY21-FY25, reflecting India's position as a global agrochemical manufacturing/export hub supported by the 'China+1' supply-chain diversification strategy, though imports of technical-grade pesticides/intermediates from China rose sharply in FY25
- India's pesticide production has remained resilient over the last five years and the long-term outlook remains positive, driven by food security requirements, modern farming adoption and demand for higher crop productivity
- Fertiliser subsidy normalisation post the FY23 peak, together with continued government policy support, is expected to support farm income and input demand

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input costs up 3-5% basket-wide (imported tech +5-6%, domestic generic +15-30%). Company plans to pass on 2% in Q1 and 3-4% in Q2. Gross margins expected to normalize ex-GST refund; carryover inventory provides temporary cushion.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend: 100% (Rs 2/share); Buyback: Up to Rs 70cr at Rs 1,400/share (~25% premium); ESOP scheme approved for employee alignment.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Dhanuka's manufacturing footprint comprises four manufacturing facilities and 41 warehouses supporting pan-India distribution. The Company operates two R&D centres, including DART (Dhanuka Agritech Research & Technology Centre) near Sihol Village, Palwal, Haryana — its flagship advanced R&D hub with laboratory infrastructure, a farmer training centre and a research farm for field trials — which is envisioned to expand further with greenhouses, polyhouses, precision spraying cabinets, pilot plant facilities, and in vivo/in vitro screening platforms. In line with its strategic objective to expand its global footprint, the Board approved incorporation of two new wholly owned subsidiaries in Brazil and a European country to facilitate transfer of brand registrations and expand product availability in those markets. During FY2025-26, the Company also secured multiple new domestic and export-only product/technical registrations from CIB&RC, widening its product and export portfolio.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and cash flows; Pragmatic on near-term margin headwinds and Dahej underperformance; Transparent on one-off benefits.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Pan-India distribution reach of ~6,500 distributors and 80,000+ retailers covering over 10 million farmers
- Strategic technology partnerships with ten multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the United States, providing access to differentiated chemistries
- In-house R&D via two R&D centres (including DART) with NABL-accredited laboratories supporting product registration, formulation development and the future growth pipeline
- Consistent flow of new product registrations from CIB&RC across both domestic and export-only categories, broadening the product portfolio

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Monsoon volatility impacting sowing; 2) Persistent input cost inflation unable to be passed through; 3) Delays in international registrations for Bayer products; 4) Regulatory changes in biostimulants.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly cited 'labor shortage' as a perpetual structural driver for herbicide demand, expanding into traditional labor-surplus states (Bihar, UP). The Dahej unit revenue guidance was downgraded to Rs 75cr for FY27 (from earlier Rs 100cr expectations) due to slow international registration despite domestic robustness.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue introducing innovative, globally relevant chemistries in India via strategic partnerships with ten multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the United States
- Strengthen in-house R&D (two R&D centres including DART, NABL-accredited laboratories) to support product registration, formulation development and the future growth pipeline
- Expand global footprint — incorporation of two new wholly owned subsidiaries in Brazil and a European country to facilitate transfer of brand registrations and product availability — alongside a growing set of export-only CIB&RC …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] The acquisition of Bayer AG's renowned fungicide brands is described as a key milestone in Dhanuka's evolution "from a domestic agrochemical leader to an emerging global player".
- [Guidance FY2026-27] Revenue from operations: "Lower Single Digit Growth"; EBITDA: "Expecting decline approx. 200bps".
- [Industry backdrop] The deck states the agrochemical industry saw a significantly challenging Q1 FY2026-27, with delayed monsoon onset postponing sowing and shifting demand from Q1 into subsequent months, and sector profitability under pressure from weaker domestic demand and price competition.
- [Incentive expiry] Incentives available to the Udhampur Unit expired in March 2026.
